This PKGBUILD follows standard AUR packaging practices for a prebuilt Electron application. The source is downloaded from the package's own declared upstream GitHub releases (`https://github.com/different-ai/openwork/releases/download/v${pkgver}/`), and checksums are properly provided for both x86_64 and aarch64 architectures (not SKIPped).

The `package()` function is straightforward: it copies the prebuilt bundle into `/opt/openwork/`, creates a symlink in `/usr/bin/`, installs an icon and a `.desktop` file, and sets the setuid bit (`chmod 4755`) on `chrome-sandbox`. The setuid on `chrome-sandbox` is the standard and required practice for Electron applications, which need a privileged helper to create Chromium's sandbox for renderer processes. This is expected behavior, not evidence of malicious intent.

The comment at the top explaining this is a template rendered by CI (`scripts/aur/update-aur.sh`) is a normal CI/CD practice for AUR packages managed through automation. There are no obfuscated commands, no unexpected network requests to unrelated hosts, no data exfiltration, and no suspicious file operations.
</details>
